newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end at record on Ericsson, Astra.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end at record on Ericsson, Astra.

text.p: Swedish shares ended at a record high on Monday, opening stronger in line with the U.S. and lifted by strong gains for bourse heavyweights telecoms group Ericsson and drugs major Astra.
The exchange's general index rose 1.14 percent to a record high of 2,608.06 in steady turnover worth 4.93 billion crowns.
Ericsson rose eight crowns to 252 ahead of releasing 1996 earnings on Tuesday and after releasing estimates of 1996 mobile phone subscribers rising 57 percent from 1995.
Astra jumped seven to 355 on recurring takeover and merger speculation.
"Talk about Astra and Zeneca has started," a trader said. Another trader said: "This is talked about regularly."
Defence group Celsius rose six crowns to 136 after releasing a preliminary 1996 pre-tax profit of 347 million crowns, higher than the company previously forecast.
Roller bearing group SKF came off day highs of 188 crowns to end the day flat at 182. During the day it kept being fuelled by posting a sharp rise in 1996 profits last week.

The forestry sector bucked positive trends and dropped 1.29 percent. Goldman Sachs confirmed on Monday it had downgraded Stora, MoDo and Rottneros to "market underperformer" from "market outperformer".
